title: The name that became a greeting
hookLine: an old teacher calls himself only the drum-beater, and the young yogi from the road gets a new name
carry: jay swaminarayan: every hello remembers god

cards: Jay Swaminarayan. In Swaminarayan homes and temples, it's how followers of this tradition say hello, how they say goodbye, and often how they answer the phone. Two words, run together into one name.
But whose name is it? The young yogi who walked into Loj didn't arrive with it. He was Ghanshyam as a child, Nilkanth on the road.
Somewhere between that ashram and the greeting on the phone, a name was given, and then a mantra. Today, how the boy from the road became Swaminarayan.

teach.b: Ramanand Swami, whose ashram Nilkanth had reached, was a respected guru in Gujarat with followers of his own. When the two met, tradition says Ramanand saw something rare in the young man.
He'd once described himself, the story goes, as only the drum-beater, the one who calls the crowd before the real performer arrives.
Ramanand initiated Nilkanth as a sadhu and gave him a new name: Sahajanand Swami, the one whose joy comes naturally. Before long, he chose this newcomer to lead the whole fellowship after him.
Tradition says that soon after Ramanand died, Sahajanand gave his followers a new name to chant: Swaminarayan. Swami, master. Narayan, a name of God.
As people chanted it, they began to call him by it too. Here the communities that follow him say different things, and say them with care.
For some, both words point to him: Sahajanand himself is Swami and Narayan, the Lord. For others, Swami names Gunatitanand Swami, whom they hold as the ideal devotee, and Narayan names Sahajanand.
They share the mantra, the greeting and the love for him.

Behind all of this sits one of Hinduism's oldest practices: japa, saying a name of God again and again, often on a mala of beads, so the mind keeps coming home to God. Followers chant Swaminarayan this way.
And the greeting carries the same idea out the front door.

teach.h: JAPA: GOD'S NAME, AGAIN AND AGAIN
teach.b: Every hello, every goodbye, every phone call is one more time the name is said.
A greeting that is also a remembering.

how: Swaminarayan followers greet one another with 'Jay Swaminarayan' and chant the Swaminarayan mantra in daily worship, remembering how Ramanand Swami initiated Nilkanth as Sahajanand Swami.

o: a tradition whose mantra became its founder's name
a tradition named for the village where it began
a tradition named after the first temple it built

games.q: from Nilkanth to Swaminarayan — tap the pairs.
p: Nilkanth's new name as a sadhu
the mantra that became his name

s: Nilkanth arrived at Loj already called Swaminarayan
Ramanand named him Sahajanand Swami, and the mantra Swaminarayan came after Ramanand's death.
every Swaminarayan community reads 'Swami' and 'Narayan' the same way
for some both words point to Sahajanand; for others Swami names Gunatitanand Swami and Narayan names Sahajanand.
followers chant Swaminarayan in japa, often on a mala of beads
repeating the name keeps the mind coming back to God; the greeting carries the same name.

games.q: you grew up in a Swaminarayan family. a new friend notices you answer every call with 'jay swaminarayan' and asks why not just 'hello'. what's the real reason?
o: it keeps God's name on your lips all day, the way japa does.
it's a password that proves you belong to the temple.
it's just habit; the words stopped meaning anything long ago.
games.why: the greeting is the mantra Sahajanand gave. saying it at the door and on the phone turns ordinary hellos into japa, remembering God.

practice: Followers of this tradition chant Swaminarayan on a mala, one bead for each name. Try it with your breath instead of beads: say a name inwardly on the in-breath, rest on the out-breath.

If you pray in this tradition, use the mantra itself; if you pray in another, a name of God you love; if you don't pray, the name of someone you're grateful for. When the mind wanders, come back to the name.

wordCard.voice: Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, how Nilkanth became Sahajanand Swami under Ramanand, and how the mantra Swaminarayan, said in japa and in every greeting, became his name. Today's word.

orig.note: Swami, 'master', and Narayan, a name of God: the mantra Sahajanand gave, which became his name.

carryVoice: Your line: jay swaminarayan, every hello remembers God. A greeting that carries a name, and a name that carries a story. Until next time.
